title: graceful-streaming-disconnect-reconnect-timeouts-openai-compat
author: Priya Malhotra
ci_details: CI pipeline: go-integration (failed on first run due to flaky reconnect test; rerun passed)
Performance benchmark: +2.3% p99 latency in worst-case reconnect path (within SLO)
description: Motivation: production streaming endpoints frequently hit issues when clients cancel, disconnect unexpectedly, or reconnect. Existing behavior was: abrupt connection tear-down -> server dropped in-flight context and KV cache for that request, leading to inconsistent partial outputs and poor UX for resumable clients. This PR implements a production-grade streaming lifecycle controller that: 1) provides an explicit client-initiated cancel API, 2) tracks transient disconnects and provides a short resume window, 3) exposes server-side idle/timeouts with configurable defaults, and 4) maps behavior into the OpenAI-compatibility layer so clients using OpenAI-like streaming semantics get predictable results. Summary of changes: - connection manager component to track per-stream state, TTLs, and resume tokens - server: accept a new X-Resume-Token header and /streams/{id}/resume endpoint to resume a recently disconnected stream - client cancel path: support a control frame (application/stream-control) and an HTTP POST /streams/{id}/cancel for non-streaming clients - idle/timeouts: default idle finalization window set to 30s (configurable via STREAM_RESUME_WINDOW), server aborts after 120s of no activity for non-resumable sessions - KV/prefix cache: retain last-kv state and token pointer for resume window; we added eviction and strict memory bounds - OpenAI compat: compatibility layer now emits the expected 'data: [DONE]' on graceful completion, and returns a 499-like code for client-abort semantics while preserving structure for function-calling and structured outputs - observability: new metrics (stream_disconnects_total, stream_resumes_total, stream_resume_failures) and traces for the resume path - tests: integration tests that simulate flaky TCP disconnects, reconnect/resume happy path, resume token mismatch, and cancel race. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default behavior does not change for long-lived non-resumable sessions. The resume window is opt-in for older clients unless they send/accept resume tokens (we added compatibility fallback in the proxy layer). Migration notes: SDKs (python/ts) will be updated in follow-up PRs to expose resume token handling and control-frame helpers. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of connection manager and server APIs - [x] Unit tests for connection state machine - [x] Integration tests (including flaky disconnect harness) - [x] OpenAI-compat mapping for streaming DONE and cancel semantics - [x] Docs page updated (streaming API reference) - [x] Benchmark run and perf validation Risks and mitigations: primary risk was increased memory usage holding KV state for resume window. We limited per-stream retained bytes to a configurable cap (STREAM_RESUME_MAX_BYTES) and added metrics/alerts. Another risk was race between cancel and resume; tests and a revision in connection manager ordering ensure cancel wins if seen before resume. If regressions observed, rollback is straightforward by toggling STREAM_RESUME_WINDOW=0 and disabling resume in config. Related work: ENG-4853 (streaming UX), ENG-4920 (observability for streaming), SUP-1287 (customer incident that motivated reconnect behavior).

review_thread: Evan Chen: The connection manager looks good. Two questions: (1) Can we avoid a global lock when marking resume state? (2) How do we prevent XSS if resume token appears in logs?
Priya Malhotra: Answered: switched to sharded locks (per-stream bucket) and resume tokens now hashed before logging; added unit test for token redaction.
Marta Rodriguez: Found a race in tests where cancel wins only sometimes. Please add deterministic ordering in the state machine.
Priya Malhotra: Addressed by making cancel path synchronous in-state transition and added a 'cancel-first' guard; updated tests accordingly.
Samir Patel: Can you add telemetry for resume failures and reason labels? We need that for SLO alerting.
Priya Malhotra: Added metrics: stream_resume_failure_reason with labels (token_mismatch, kv_evicted, timeout, internal_error) and hooked into tracing.
Evan Chen: Approving after CI stable run. Left one nit about documentation sample for ts-sdk — suggest a short snippet.
Priya Malhotra: Added TS example snippet in docs. Marking ready to merge.
release_notes: Streaming: add graceful disconnect/reconnect and client cancel. New resume-token header and /streams/{id}/resume endpoint enable short-window resume for interrupted streams. Default behavior remains compatible; resume is opt-in. Observability: new streaming resume/disconnect metrics. See docs/reference/streaming.md for usage.
